follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Reddit lost $3.59 for every $100 of revenue this quarter.
footerNote: Figures are from Reddit's Q2 2024 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q, which report in thousands. Reddit's tax line was a $0.22M benefit this quarter. The 10-Q says income tax expense (benefit) was immaterial and that Reddit continues to maintain a full valuation allowance on its remaining federal and state deferred tax assets — it still carries large tax losses from earlier years, so it pays almost no income tax.

otherDetail: Other income of $20.7M, net — $20.9M of interest income, net, earned on Reddit's $1,699.1M of cash and marketable securities, less $0.2M of other expense, net. Interest income is what narrowed a $31.0M operating loss to a $10.3M pre-tax loss.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — powered by more impressions delivered as users surged, partly offset by lower pricing.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly data licensing — deals that let AI companies train on Reddit's public posts — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions. Up nearly eight-fold from just $3.5M a year ago as the licensing deals executed in 2024 kicked in.

takeaways.text: Daily Active Uniques reached 91.2 million, up 51% from 60.4 million a year ago, and Weekly Active Uniques rose 57% to 342.3 million — the audience growth behind the 41% jump in ad revenue.
takeaways.title: Daily users surged 51%

takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $39.5 million, a 14.0% margin, up $74.9 million from -$35.4 million a year ago. The net loss also narrowed to $10.1 million from $41.1 million a year ago, with gross margin improving to 89.5% from 84.2%.
takeaways.title: Adjusted EBITDA turned strongly positive

takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation was $64.3 million in the quarter — $66.8 million including related taxes — more than six times the $10.1 million net loss and 23% of revenue. That gap is why Adjusted EBITDA looks so much stronger than the GAAP loss; this quarter's charge is the normal post-IPO run rate, not the Q1 2024 IPO catch-up charge.
takeaways.title: Stock pay still dwarfs the result

verdict: Reddit's revenue grew 54% to $281M as daily users jumped 51% to 91.2 million, cutting its net loss to just $10M — but stock pay kept it in the red on a GAAP basis.
